Tufelli_masonry_typeA.name: Tufelli_masonry_typeA
Tufelli_masonry_typeA._evidence: A-419/a419 photos (WhatsApp Image 2023-06-01 at 14.50.49/50/51): stone arch over a door with well-dressed voussoirs, courses fairly regular though not perfectly continuous
_flags: Vertical joint staggering scored 'partially_staggered' (conservative) rather than 'properly_staggered' - not directly measurable from the available photos at typical phone-camera resolution/angle

Mortar scored plain 'lime' (conservative) rather than crediting the pozzolana content mentioned in the manuscript with a hydraulic-lime-level score - the pozzolana's real contribution to mortar performance was not tested, only described qualitatively

Tufelli_masonry_typeD.name: Tufelli_masonry_typeD
Tufelli_masonry_typeD._evidence: A-417/417_b (WhatsApp Image 2023-06-01 at 14.51.52/53) and A-420/a420 (WhatsApp Image 2023-06-01 at 14.50.52-55): fully plastered in every available survey photo, no exposed masonry
_flags: ENTIRELY assumed, not observed: scored identically to typeB (the 'ordinary/irregular' type) as the most defensible default for an unexceptional rendered facade in the same aggregate, rather than typeA (visibly higher quality, tied to specific observed stonework at door openings that this facade's render gives no evidence for) or typeC (visibly patched/reworked, again no evidence either way). This is the weakest-grounded of the four classifications - revisit first if render is ever removed, or if there is independent reason (archival, structural survey) to place this facade in a specific construction phase.
